narrative.overview:
NeighbourHood uses its incumbent teal identity, warm stone ground, white surfaces and system UI typography to make local inventory and the next action easy to read. This is the implemented visual system for the resident and volunteer web app, recorded after the approved enhancement. It preserves the existing identity rather than introducing a new art direction.

The interface is compact but gives controls and supporting copy room. Actual item photos provide visual detail; absent or broken photos receive an honest outline-icon fallback. Browsing expands on wider screens while forms and conversations retain a readable measure. The approved surface composition remains in `.impeccable/surfaces/src-app-tsx.md`; this document records reusable visual rules rather than prescribing Home's layout for every route.

The follow-up uses labelled icon pills for utilities and one attachment + beside the Ask textarea. Missing search coordinates produce an explicit setup state; pending data retains item-shaped skeletons. Explore opens a map of the resident's saved point and radius directly below its title, with search and filters underneath. Home shortcuts precede Nearby items, and a native category dropdown follows All / Free / Borrow. The map retains provider disclosure, attribution, hide and retry. Existing palette, type and spacing tokens remain unchanged.

Ask is a raised 48px teal navigation action with its visible label retained. Explore places a manual 1–50 km distance control between map and item search. Product pins group rounded public areas into numbered teardrop markers; popups reveal matching item links. Ask result cards state the checked radius, separate farther matches and draft editable radius replies. The seed includes bundled generated product photos for matched sample records; these are test content, not evidence of actual inventory.

Ask streams real assistant text and progress, with Stop and durable history recovery. New tasks clarify the next missing fact with one casual question per turn, answered through the normal composer. Optional quick replies draft an editable answer. Older product results collapse and retain their photos and bookmark controls without stale radius prompts. Human messages show product thumbnails and support private photo attachments. Saved items bookmark actual listings, separate from Saved needs. Selected photos preview during upload and remain with the first message, private draft and publication approval card. Failed uploads retain retry/remove controls and block incomplete sends. Publication can be prepared conversationally using the saved Profile pickup area, and executes only after explicit confirmation.
keyCharacteristics: Teal actions over a quiet stone and white field.
Clear system typography, sentence-case controls and descriptive supporting copy.
Restrained borders, rounded surfaces and consistent outline SVG icons.
Mobile discovery grids, readable conversations and explicit state changes.

rules.name: The Action Teal Rule
rules.body: Use the existing teal family for actions, focus and selected states; retain words alongside semantic status colors.

rules.name: The One Type Voice Rule
rules.body: Extend the established system sans hierarchy instead of adding a display face to ordinary product screens.

rules.name: The Quiet Surface Rule
rules.body: Separate ordinary surfaces with tone and thin edges; preserve the existing flat card and button treatment.

dos: Do reuse the existing teal, stone, white and system sans vocabulary.
Do keep meaningful supporting copy readable and use words alongside colored states.
Do match pending skeleton geometry to its eventual content and give empty results a concrete next step.
Do retain public area and distance together, while keeping exact pickup information behind its authorized flow.
Do keep the conversation scroll region, composer and bottom tabs structurally separate.
Do use actual item photos and honest no-photo fallbacks.
donts: Don't introduce a new visual identity, display family or decorative elevation for ordinary product screens.
Don't turn nested content into repeated bordered cards; preserve the implemented flattening rule.
Don't imply that Borrow is date-available, that a public area is verified, or that an unconfirmed action has completed.
Don't use synthetic item imagery or invented counts as evidence of live inventory or unread activity.
